title: UP BOARD CLASS 9 — Social Science | Working of Institutions Parliament
description: Subject-wise test on Working of Institutions Parliament (Social Science) for UP BOARD CLASS 9. 50Q.
subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: Which of the following institutions is primarily responsible for making laws in India?

options.text: The Judiciary
options.explanation: The Judiciary is responsible for interpreting laws, not making them.

options.text: The Executive
options.explanation: The Executive is responsible for implementing laws, not making them.

options.text: The Parliament
options.explanation: The Parliament is the supreme legislative body in India responsible for enacting laws.

options.text: The Election Commission
options.explanation: The Election Commission is responsible for conducting elections, not making laws.

questions.explanation: The Parliament, consisting of the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha, is the supreme legislative body in India responsible for enacting laws.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: In India, who among the following is considered the head of the government?

options.text: The President
options.explanation: The President is the head of the state, not the head of the government.

options.text: The Chief Justice of India
options.explanation: The Chief Justice of India is the head of the judiciary, not the head of the government.

options.text: The Prime Minister
options.explanation: The Prime Minister is the head of the government and wields most of the executive powers.

options.text: The Speaker of Lok Sabha
options.explanation: The Speaker of Lok Sabha is the presiding officer of the Lok Sabha, not the head of the government.

questions.explanation: While the President is the head of the state, the Prime Minister is the head of the government and wields most of the executive powers.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: What was the main recommendation of the Mandal Commission, which led to significant institutional decisions in India?

options.text: Reservation of seats for women in Parliament
options.explanation: The Mandal Commission did not recommend reservation of seats for women in Parliament.

options.text: Reservation of 27% of government jobs for Socially and Educationally Backward Classes (SEBCs)
options.explanation: The Mandal Commission recommended 27% reservation for Other Backward Classes (OBCs) in central government jobs and public sector undertakings.

options.text: Introduction of the Goods and Services Tax (GST)
options.explanation: The Mandal Commission did not recommend the introduction of the Goods and Services Tax (GST).

options.text: Establishment of a new judicial system
options.explanation: The Mandal Commission did not recommend the establishment of a new judicial system.

questions.explanation: The Mandal Commission recommended 27% reservation for Other Backward Classes (OBCs) in central government jobs and public sector undertakings, which was implemented in 1990.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha is correct?

options.text: The Rajya Sabha has more power in money matters than the Lok Sabha.
options.explanation: The Lok Sabha has more power in money matters than the Rajya Sabha.

options.text: A no-confidence motion can be moved in both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha.
options.explanation: A no-confidence motion can only be moved in the Lok Sabha.

options.text: The Lok Sabha is more powerful than the Rajya Sabha in passing ordinary laws.
options.explanation: The Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha have equal powers in passing ordinary laws.

options.text: The Lok Sabha can control the Council of Ministers by passing a no-confidence motion.
options.explanation: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. If a no-confidence motion is passed in the Lok Sabha, the government must resign.

questions.explanation: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. If a no-confidence motion is passed in the Lok Sabha, the government must resign. The Rajya Sabha does not have this power.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: What is the primary function of the 'permanent executive' in a democracy like India?

options.text: To represent the political will of the ruling party.
options.explanation: The permanent executive does not represent the political will of the ruling party.

options.text: To formulate new policies and laws.
options.explanation: The permanent executive does not formulate new policies and laws.

options.text: To assist the ministers in implementing policies and administering the country.
options.explanation: The permanent executive assists the ministers in implementing policies and administering the country.

options.text: To approve international treaties and agreements.
options.explanation: The permanent executive does not approve international treaties and agreements.

questions.explanation: The permanent executive refers to the civil servants or bureaucrats who are experts in administration and assist the politically elected ministers in the day-to-day running and implementation of government policies.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the President of India: 1. The President is the Head of the State. 2. The President exercises executive powers only on the advice of the Council of Ministers. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.text: Only 1
options.explanation: Both statements are correct.

options.text: Only 2
options.explanation: Both statements are correct.

options.text: Both 1 and 2
options.explanation: The President is indeed the constitutional head of the state and exercises executive powers only on the advice of the Council of Ministers.

options.text: Neither 1 nor 2
options.explanation: Both statements are correct.

questions.explanation: The President is indeed the constitutional head of the state. According to the Indian Constitution, the President acts on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: Assertion (A): An independent judiciary is essential for a democratic country. Reason (R): It protects the fundamental rights of citizens and ensures that laws are applied equally and fairly. Which of the following is correct?

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The assertion is true and the reason correctly explains it.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: The reason is true and correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: The assertion is true and the reason correctly explains it.

questions.explanation: The assertion is true as judicial independence safeguards the rule of law. The reason correctly explains that this independence allows the judiciary to act impartially, protect rights, and ensure fair application of laws, thus making R the correct explanation for A.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: When no single party gets a clear majority in the Lok Sabha elections, two or more parties may come together to form the government. This type of government is known as a:

options.text: Caretaker government
options.explanation: A caretaker government is a temporary government that is formed to oversee the administration of a country until a new government is formed.

options.text: Minority government
options.explanation: A minority government is a government that is formed by a party that does not have a majority in the legislature, but is able to govern with the support of other parties.

options.text: Coalition government
options.explanation: A coalition government is formed when multiple political parties agree to cooperate and form a government because no single party has achieved an absolute majority in the legislature.

options.text: Provisional government
options.explanation: A provisional government is a temporary government that is formed to oversee the administration of a country until a new government is formed.

questions.explanation: A coalition government is formed when multiple political parties agree to cooperate and form a government because no single party has achieved an absolute majority in the legislature.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: A group of citizens feels that a newly passed law by the Parliament violates a provision of the Constitution. Which institution has the power to review this law and declare it unconstitutional if found to be so?

options.text: The Prime Minister
options.explanation: The Prime Minister does not have the power of judicial review.

options.text: The President
options.explanation: The President does not have the power of judicial review.

options.text: The Supreme Court
options.explanation: The Supreme Court has the power of 'judicial review,' which allows it to examine the constitutionality of laws passed by the legislature and actions of the executive.

options.text: The Comptroller and Auditor General
options.explanation: The Comptroller and Auditor General does not have the power of judicial review.

questions.explanation: The Supreme Court has the power of 'judicial review,' which allows it to examine the constitutionality of laws passed by the legislature and actions of the executive.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: For a bill to become a law in India, after being passed by both Houses of Parliament, whose assent is required?

options.text: The Speaker of Lok Sabha
options.explanation: The Speaker of Lok Sabha does not have the power to assent to a bill.

options.text: The Chief Justice of India
options.explanation: The Chief Justice of India does not have the power to assent to a bill.

options.text: The Vice-President
options.explanation: The Vice-President does not have the power to assent to a bill.

options.text: The President
options.explanation: A bill passed by both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha must receive the President's assent to be enacted as a law (Act).

questions.explanation: A bill passed by both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha must receive the President's assent to be enacted as a law (Act).
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: What was the primary recommendation of the Mandal Commission Report, which became a significant policy decision in India?

options.text: Reservation of seats for women in Parliament.
options.explanation: This was not the primary recommendation of the Mandal Commission Report.

options.text: 27% reservation for Socially and Educationally Backward Classes (SEBCs) in government jobs.
options.explanation: This was the primary recommendation of the Mandal Commission Report.

options.text: Abolition of the Zamindari system.
options.explanation: The Mandal Commission Report did not recommend the abolition of the Zamindari system.

options.text: Universalisation of primary education.
options.explanation: The Mandal Commission Report did not recommend the universalisation of primary education.

questions.explanation: The Mandal Commission Report, submitted in 1980, recommended 27% reservation for SEBCs in central government services, which was later implemented.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: Which of the following bodies is considered the supreme law-making institution in India?

options.text: The Supreme Court
options.explanation: The Supreme Court is the highest judicial body in India, but it is not the supreme law-making institution.

options.text: The President's Secretariat
options.explanation: The President's Secretariat is an administrative body that assists the President, but it is not the supreme law-making institution.

options.text: The Parliament
options.explanation: The Parliament is the supreme law-making institution in India.

options.text: The Prime Minister's Office
options.explanation: The Prime Minister's Office is an administrative body that assists the Prime Minister, but it is not the supreme law-making institution.

questions.explanation: The Parliament is the final authority for making laws in India, consisting of the President, Lok Sabha, and Rajya Sabha.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: Despite being the Head of State, the President of India is often referred to as a 'nominal executive'. What is the main reason for this?

options.text: The President is directly elected by the people of India.
options.explanation: The President is not directly elected by the people of India.

options.text: The President exercises all powers only on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.
options.explanation: This is the main reason why the President is referred to as a 'nominal executive'.

options.text: The President has the power to dismiss the Prime Minister at any time.
options.explanation: The President does not have the power to dismiss the Prime Minister at any time.

options.text: The President's decisions require the approval of the Chief Justice of India.
options.explanation: The President's decisions do not require the approval of the Chief Justice of India.

questions.explanation: The President's role is largely ceremonial and nominal because, in a parliamentary democracy, the real executive power rests with the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers, whose advice the President is bound to follow.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: Who among the following is the Head of the Government in India?

options.text: Prime Minister
options.explanation: The Prime Minister is the Head of the Government in India.

options.text: President
options.explanation: The President is the Head of State, not the Head of the Government.

options.text: Chief Justice of India
options.explanation: The Chief Justice of India is the head of the judiciary, not the Head of the Government.

options.text: Speaker of Lok Sabha
options.explanation: The Speaker of Lok Sabha is the presiding officer of the Lok Sabha, not the Head of the Government.

questions.explanation: The Prime Minister is the Head of the Government and leads the Council of Ministers, holding the real executive power. The President is the Head of State.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: Regarding a 'money bill', which statement accurately describes the powers of the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha?

options.text: Money bills can only be introduced in the Rajya Sabha.
options.explanation: Money bills can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha.

options.text: The Lok Sabha has more powers regarding money bills and can override the Rajya Sabha's recommendations.
options.explanation: The Lok Sabha has more powers regarding money bills and can override the Rajya Sabha's recommendations.

options.text: Both houses have equal powers in passing money bills.
options.explanation: The Lok Sabha has more powers regarding money bills than the Rajya Sabha.

options.text: Money bills require a joint sitting of both houses for approval if there is a disagreement.
options.explanation: Money bills do not require a joint sitting of both houses for approval if there is a disagreement.

questions.explanation: Money bills can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha. The Rajya Sabha can only delay a money bill for a maximum of 14 days or suggest amendments, which the Lok Sabha is not bound to accept.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: Assertion (A): The Prime Minister is the most important political institution in the country. Reason (R): The Prime Minister is the head of the government and leads the Council of Ministers, making most of the policy decisions.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both Assertion A and Reason R are true, and Reason R correctly explains Assertion A.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Reason R is the correct explanation of Assertion A.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Both Assertion A and Reason R are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: Both Assertion A and Reason R are true.

questions.explanation: The Prime Minister is indeed the most important political institution because they are the head of government and hold significant executive power, leading the decision-making process through the Council of Ministers. Reason R correctly explains Assertion A.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: What is the main role of the Parliament in controlling the executive (government)?

options.text: To appoint the Chief Justice of India.
options.explanation: The appointment of the Chief Justice of India is not the main role of the Parliament in controlling the executive.

options.text: To issue executive orders for policy implementation.
options.explanation: The Parliament does not issue executive orders for policy implementation.

options.text: To pass laws, approve budgets, and hold ministers accountable through debates and questions.
options.explanation: This is the main role of the Parliament in controlling the executive.

options.text: To directly implement government schemes and policies.
options.explanation: The Parliament does not directly implement government schemes and policies.

questions.explanation: Parliament exercises control over the government by making laws, approving the budget (financial control), and holding ministers accountable through various parliamentary devices like questions, debates, and no-confidence motions.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: After a bill has been passed by both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha, what is the next essential step for it to become a law?

options.text: It needs the approval of the Supreme Court.
options.explanation: The approval of the Supreme Court is not required for a bill to become a law.

options.text: It must be signed by the Prime Minister.
options.explanation: The signature of the Prime Minister is not required for a bill to become a law.

options.text: It requires the assent of the President.
options.explanation: The assent of the President is required for a bill to become a law.

options.text: It needs to be published in the national newspapers.
options.explanation: Publication in national newspapers is not required for a bill to become a law.

questions.explanation: A bill passed by both Houses of Parliament becomes an Act (law) only after receiving the assent of the President, who is an integral part of the Parliament.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: Consider the following scenario: A major policy decision regarding agricultural subsidies is taken by the government. Who is primarily responsible for the implementation of this policy, once it has been approved at the highest political level?

options.text: The President of India
options.explanation: The President of India is not responsible for the implementation of policies.

options.text: The Supreme Court
options.explanation: The Supreme Court is not responsible for the implementation of policies.

options.text: The Lok Sabha
options.explanation: The Lok Sabha is not responsible for the implementation of policies.

options.text: The Civil Servants (bureaucracy)
options.explanation: The civil servants or bureaucracy are responsible for the implementation of policies.

questions.explanation: While the political executive (Cabinet, Ministers) takes the decision, the permanent executive, i.e., the civil servants or bureaucracy, are responsible for working out the details, drafting rules, and actually implementing the policies on the ground.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: How are the members of the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) elected?

options.text: Directly by the people through universal adult franchise.
options.explanation: The members of the Rajya Sabha are not elected directly by the people.

options.text: Indirectly by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies.
options.explanation: The members of the Rajya Sabha are elected indirectly by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies.

options.text: Nominated by the Prime Minister.
options.explanation: The members of the Rajya Sabha are not nominated by the Prime Minister.

options.text: Elected by the Chief Ministers of all states.
options.explanation: The members of the Rajya Sabha are not elected by the Chief Ministers of all states.

questions.explanation: The members of the Rajya Sabha are primarily elected indirectly by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies using the system of proportional representation with a single transferable vote.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: Which among the following is NOT a function of the Parliament of India?

options.text: Making laws on subjects in the Union List
options.explanation: This is a function of the Parliament of India.

options.text: Approving the Union Budget
options.explanation: This is a function of the Parliament of India.

options.text: Appointing the Chief Justice of India
options.explanation: The appointment of the Chief Justice of India is done by the President of India.

options.text: Exercising control over the Council of Ministers
options.explanation: This is a function of the Parliament of India.

questions.explanation: The appointment of the Chief Justice of India is done by the President of India in consultation with the current Chief Justice and other senior judges, not by the Parliament.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: Read the following statements about the Lok Sabha and identify the correct one:

options.text: The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is 552 members
options.explanation: Although this statement is true, it is not the correct answer according to the provided explanation.

options.text: The Lok Sabha can be dissolved by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister
options.explanation: The Lok Sabha can be dissolved by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister.

options.text: The term of the Lok Sabha is fixed at 6 years
options.explanation: The term of the Lok Sabha is 5 years, not 6 years.

options.text: Only elected members of the Rajya Sabha can become its Speaker
options.explanation: The Speaker is elected from among the members of the Lok Sabha, not Rajya Sabha.

questions.explanation: The Lok Sabha can be dissolved by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Rajya Sabha is correct?

options.text: It is a temporary body that dissolves every 3 years
options.explanation: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body.

options.text: Its members are directly elected by the people of India
options.explanation: The members of the Rajya Sabha are elected indirectly by the elected members of State Legislative Assemblies.

options.text: One-third of its members retire every two years
options.explanation: One-third of the Rajya Sabha members retire every two years.

options.text: It has equal powers with the Lok Sabha in all matters
options.explanation: The Rajya Sabha does not have equal powers with the Lok Sabha in all matters.

questions.explanation: One-third of the Rajya Sabha members retire every two years.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: Consider the following statements about the Parliament:

options.text: Only Statement I
options.explanation: During a National Emergency, the Parliament can make laws on any subject, including those in the State List.

options.text: Only Statement II
options.explanation: Statement II is not entirely correct as the Parliament can make laws on State List subjects during a National Emergency.

options.text: Both I and II
options.explanation: Statement II is not entirely correct as the Parliament can make laws on State List subjects during a National Emergency.

options.text: Neither I nor II
options.explanation: Statement I is correct.

questions.explanation: During a National Emergency, the Parliament can make laws on any subject.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

options.explanation: The correct match is: Public Accounts Committee - examines the audit reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General, Estimates Committee - examines the budgetary provisions before they are voted, Committee on Public Undertakings - examines the working of public sector undertakings, Business Advisory Committee - screens bills and allocates time for discussion.

questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: Assertion (A): The Parliament can remove the President of India through the process of impeachment. Reason (R): The President can be impeached for violation of the Constitution.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.explanation: The President can be impeached for violation of the Constitution, and the process involves the Parliament.

options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.explanation: R is the correct explanation of A.

options.text: A is true but R is false
options.explanation: R is true, the President can be impeached for violation of the Constitution.

options.text: A is false but R is true
options.explanation: A is true, the Parliament can remove the President of India through the process of impeachment.

questions.explanation: The President can be impeached for violation of the Constitution, and the process involves the Parliament.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a qualification required to become a member of the Lok Sabha?

options.text: Must be a citizen of India
options.explanation: This is a required qualification as per Article 84 of the Constitution.

options.text: Must be at least 25 years of age
options.explanation: This is a required qualification as per Article 84 of the Constitution.

options.text: Must be a graduate from a recognized university
options.explanation: The Constitution does not require a graduate degree to become a member of the Lok Sabha.

options.text: Must be registered as a voter in any parliamentary constituency
options.explanation: This is a required qualification as per Article 84 of the Constitution.

questions.explanation: The Constitution does not require a graduate degree to become a member of the Lok Sabha. The other options are qualifications as per Article 84 of the Constitution.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: During the Monsoon Session of Parliament, a bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha. After discussion, it was referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee. However, the Committee could not submit its report before the end of the session. What is the most likely next step for the bill?

options.text: The bill will automatically lapse
options.explanation: The bill will lapse if it is not a Money Bill.

options.text: The bill will be sent to the President for assent
options.explanation: The bill must be passed by both Houses before it can be sent to the President for assent.

options.text: The bill will be reintroduced in the next session
options.explanation: Although this may happen, it is not the most likely next step.

options.text: The bill will be sent to the Supreme Court for review
options.explanation: The bill does not need to be sent to the Supreme Court for review at this stage.

questions.explanation: If a bill is referred to a committee and the committee cannot submit its report before the session ends, the bill usually lapses and must be reintroduced in the next session. It does not lapse automatically if it is a Money Bill.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Speaker of the Lok Sabha is INCORRECT?

options.text: The Speaker is elected by the members of the Lok Sabha
options.explanation: This statement is correct.

options.text: The Speaker remains in office until the Lok Sabha is dissolved
options.explanation: The Speaker can be removed by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the House.

options.text: The Speaker presides over the joint sittings of both Houses
options.explanation: This statement is correct.

options.text: The Speaker can allow a suspended member to participate in proceedings after the suspension period
options.explanation: This statement is correct.

questions.explanation: The Speaker remains in office until the Lok Sabha is dissolved only if the Speaker is not removed earlier. The Speaker can be removed by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the House.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: Which of the following is a discretionary power of the President of India in relation to the Parliament?

options.text: Summoning and proroguing the sessions of Parliament
options.explanation: The President must exercise this power on the advice of the Council of Ministers.

options.text: Addressing either House of Parliament or both Houses assembled together
options.explanation: The President must exercise this power on the advice of the Council of Ministers.

options.text: Returning a non-Money Bill for reconsideration
options.explanation: The President has discretionary power to return a non-Money Bill for reconsideration by the Parliament.

options.text: Appointing the Prime Minister
options.explanation: The President must exercise this power on the advice of the Council of Ministers.

questions.explanation: The President has discretionary power to return a non-Money Bill for reconsideration by the Parliament. This is not applicable to Money Bills. The other options are powers that the President must exercise on the advice of the Council of Ministers.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: Which among the following is NOT a function of the Parliament in India?

options.text: Making laws for the country
options.explanation: This is a function of the Parliament.

options.text: Controlling the government’s expenditure
options.explanation: This is a function of the Parliament.

options.text: Appointing the Chief Justice of India
options.explanation: The President appoints the Chief Justice of India after consultation with senior judges.

options.text: Discussing and debating issues of public importance
options.explanation: This is a function of the Parliament.

questions.explanation: The Parliament does not appoint the Chief Justice of India; this is done by the President after consultation with senior judges.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: The Rajya Sabha can delay a Money Bill for a maximum period of:

options.text: 14 days
options.explanation: The Rajya Sabha must return a Money Bill within 14 days.

options.text: 30 days
options.explanation: This is not the correct time period.

options.text: 6 months
options.explanation: This is not the correct time period.

options.text: 1 year
options.explanation: This is not the correct time period.

questions.explanation: According to Article 109 of the Constitution, the Rajya Sabha can only recommend amendments to a Money Bill and must return it within 14 days.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: Assertion (A): The President of India is a part of the Parliament. Reason (R): The President is the head of the state and part of the Union Executive, which functions within the constitutional framework of Parliament.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.explanation: The President is part of the Parliament and the reason explains this fact.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
options.explanation: The reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: A is true, but R is false
options.explanation: The reason is true and explains the assertion.

options.text: A is false, but R is true
options.explanation: The assertion is true and the reason explains it.

questions.explanation: The President is indeed a part of the Parliament as per the constitutional provisions, and the reason correctly explains this fact.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: The Parliament can make laws on subjects in the State List during:

options.text: National Emergency
options.explanation: During a National Emergency, Parliament can make laws on State List subjects.

options.text: Financial Emergency
options.explanation: This is not the correct condition.

options.text: Failure of Constitutional Machinery in a State
options.explanation: This is not the correct condition.

options.text: All of the above
options.explanation: Only National Emergency is the correct condition.

questions.explanation: Under Article 352 (National Emergency), Parliament can legislate on State List subjects.
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Speaker of the Lok Sabha is correct?

options.text: The Speaker remains in office during the pleasure of the President
options.explanation: The Speaker can be removed by a resolution.

options.text: The Speaker can be removed by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the Lok Sabha
options.explanation: The Speaker can be removed by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members.

options.text: The Speaker’s salary is fixed by the Constitution
options.explanation: This is not the correct statement about the Speaker.

options.text: The Speaker has no vote in the House
options.explanation: This is not the correct statement about the Speaker.

questions.explanation: The Speaker can be removed by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the Lok Sabha (absolute majority).
questions.subject: upbo9-sst

questions.question: A Member of Parliament raises a question regarding the non-utilization of funds allocated for rural development in his constituency. The concerned minister provides a written reply stating that the funds were diverted due to unforeseen calamities. Which parliamentary device is being used here?

options.text: Adjournment Motion
options.explanation: This is not the correct parliamentary device.

options.text: Calling Attention Notice
